newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * President Ion Iliescu has officially registered his candidacy for the November 3 elections with the Central Electoral Bureau (BEC).
BEC sources said Iliescu's supporters gathered more than 400,000 to back his candidacy.
* The deadline for registering presidential candidacies expires 30 days before the polls, said BEC chairman, judge Costica Ionescu.
* Senate voted rail transport bill which splits the SNCFR authority into railway administrators and rolling stock operators, allowing infrastructure to be used by state or private rail operators.
* Lower Chamber of Deputies resumed debates on bill to amend the penal code. Deputies discussed article no 200 on homosexual relations.
Greater Romania Party and National Unity Party MPs quoted religious and health arguments to demand that homosexual relations be punished with jail terms.

National Peasant Party deputies asked that "public scandal" -- used in previous version to designate cases when homosexual relations can be punished -- be dropped from bill, saying it was ambiguous and might raise problems in law enforcement.
Debates on the bill were adjourned for Monday, Sept 9.
* Social Democratic Union (USD) and miners' confederation struk deal to support each other's interests ahead of polls.
USD pledged to promote confederation's strategy to restructure the mining sector and reconvert labour force.
* Professor George Muntean launched his candidacy for presidential elections on behalf of the Pensioners' Party.
* Romania should be cautious in privatising its energy sector, political leaders said during the second day of International conference on restructuring the industry.
* Romania is not prepared to privatise its energy sector, said leading businessman George Paunescu. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
